scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-01.statement: Field manual-read route completion was 0.88 against a 0.95 target for 9,200 accounts over Aug-Sep 2026.

F-02.statement: Dispute ticket response times (2,440 tickets) over the surge period were median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, both within the 3.0-day SLA target.

F-03.statement: Of 3,025 disputed bills, 1,240 were on ESTIMATED reads and 1,785 were on ACTUAL reads.

F-04.statement: Billing-db's tariff_change_log contains zero records this year, authoritatively confirming no tariff change occurred.

F-06.statement: route-log identifies 14 lagging manual-read routes, each with a distinct completion value (sample: route R-00 at 0.70 completion).

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING.statement: Dispute surge is primarily a ticket-handling/response-speed problem, so an AI agent that auto-answers tickets and auto-corrects bills would resolve it.

H-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August introduced systematic errors that cause bills to be wrong, driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-EXPORT-GAP.statement: Degraded AMI read delivery or MDMS export reliability around August caused missing reads, triggering estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-GAP.statement: A decline in manual field meter read completion or handoff quality around August caused missing reads, triggering estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-ESTIMATE-LOGIC-FLAW.statement: The estimate-substitution logic used when no accepted read is available is itself flawed or over-triggered, producing wrong bills independent of upstream read-delivery health.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route completion for manual-read accounts was 88% against a 95% target over Aug-Sep 2026, covering 9,200 accounts — a real shortfall in manual meter-read collection coincident with the dispute surge window. This is a concrete operational gap, not merely a ticket-handling/response-speed symptom.

E-02 shows CRM dispute-ticket handling (2,440 tickets) is running well within SLA: median response 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, both under the 3.0-day target. This is response-handling performance data; it says nothing about why bills are wrong, but it directly tests whether slow ticket handling is the surge driver.

E-03 splits the 3,025 disputed bills by meter-read type: 1,240 used ESTIMATED reads and 1,785 used ACTUAL reads. This means the majority (59%) of disputed bills came from bills built on real actual reads, not from the estimate-substitution path, so causes rooted purely in missing reads (AMI export gap, field read gap) explain only a minority of the disputed population; something affecting bills with actual reads too must also be in play.

E-04.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) claims no tariff change occurred this year. This is an unverified stakeholder statement, not authoritative data, and bears only on whether a tariff change is a contributing cause of wrong bills — a question distinct from the billing import validation-rule change tracked by DA-RULES.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager, who has an incentive toward a contract headcount increase and a documented bias to attribute problems to staffing) claims the team has been short three readers since July, causing late routes and estimated bills for affected customers. This is an unverified causal claim offering a mechanism consistent with the already-confirmed route completion shortfall (E-01), but it needs independent corroboration before being treated as the cause.

E-06 is an authoritative, complete billing-db query of the tariff_change_log returning zero records, meaning no tariff change was logged this year. This upgrades the previously unverified stakeholder claims (CL-02 from SH-BILL, E-04) from non-authoritative to authoritatively confirmed, closing the tariff-change line of inquiry; it does not speak to the separate billing import validation-rule change (DA-RULES) that H-RULE-CHANGE concerns.

CRM dispute_volume_monthly shows 610 and 590 tickets in Jun/Jul 2026 (pre-surge baseline, ~600/mo) rising to 1180 and 1260 in Aug/Sep 2026 — roughly a doubling, authoritatively confirming the magnitude and timing of the surge referenced in the initial request. This is pure volume data; it says nothing about what caused the wrong bills or whether handling speed is the driver.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: This contract clause establishes that route priority changes may be requested by the utility but must be executed only after Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) confirmation. It is a procedural/authorization document, not causal evidence about why bills are wrong or disputes surged.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log's lagging_routes query returns 14 distinct manual-read routes each with its own completion rate (sample: R-00 at 0.70), giving route-level granularity on the completion shortfall already seen in aggregate (E-01). This confirms the shortfall is spread across multiple routes rather than being a single anomaly, but it is still route-completion data, not independent staffing evidence, so it does not by itself verify reader shortage as the cause.

U-RULE-CHANGE-MECHANISM.question: Does the billing import validation rule change log (DA-RULES) show a change around August explaining ACTUAL-read bill errors, versus the estimate-substitution logic itself being flawed (H-RULE-CHANGE vs H-ESTIMATE-LOGIC-FLAW)?
U-RULE-CHANGE-MECHANISM.decision_impact: Determines whether a fix would target billing import validation rules or estimate-substitution logic; until resolved, no bill-correction action can be authorized or targeted correctly.
U-RULE-CHANGE-MECHANISM.resolution_path: Run the billing-config rule-change log query over the Aug 2026 window and compare rule-change timestamps against the onset of ACTUAL-read disputes.
U-RULE-CHANGE-MECHANISM.safe_placeholder: Perform the rule-log review as a diagnostic-only step; propose no bill correction until the mechanism is confirmed.

U-AMI-EXPORT-ACCESS.question: Will vendor-provisioned MDMS export access become available to directly check AMI read-event delivery health, which the current elimination logic (E-03) only indirectly addresses?
U-AMI-EXPORT-ACCESS.decision_impact: Without direct AMI read-event data, conclusions about read-delivery health rely solely on the indirect billing-side read-type split (E-03).
U-AMI-EXPORT-ACCESS.resolution_path: Request ORG-AMI (vendor) to provision mdms-export access; re-run a direct AMI read-event query once mdms-export tool health is no longer DEGRADED.
U-AMI-EXPORT-ACCESS.safe_placeholder: Continue relying on the billing-db read-type elimination logic (E-03) in place of direct AMI verification until vendor access is restored.

U-FIELD-STAFFING-CAUSE.question: Is the field reader shortage (SH-FIELD's claim, E-05) an independently corroborated cause of the route-completion shortfall (E-01), or just an unverified, incentive-biased explanation?
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CAUSE.decision_impact: If the staffing claim is not corroborated, a route-update fix aimed at staffing could address the wrong lever, leaving the real cause of the shortfall unaddressed.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CAUSE.resolution_path: Independently corroborate SH-FIELD's staffing claim (E-05) against field-ops headcount/scheduling records, given SH-FIELD's documented incentive bias toward a contract headcount increase.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Treat the staffing shortage as an unverified contributing factor; limit any route change to the diagnostic corroboration step until independently confirmed.

U-METRIC-VALIDITY.question: Would an auto-answering ticket agent reduce dispute ticket volume without actually improving bill accuracy, invalidating ticket-volume alone as the success measure?
U-METRIC-VALIDITY.decision_impact: If ticket volume can fall without bill accuracy improving, dispute-volume-trend alone is an invalid success measure and the project could be declared successful incorrectly.
U-METRIC-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Track the actual_read_dispute_share metric alongside dispute_volume_trend so any volume reduction is corroborated by a reduced share of ACTUAL-read disputes, not just fewer tickets filed.
U-METRIC-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Report dispute-volume trend together with actual-read dispute share; do not declare success on volume reduction alone.
